To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the condensation of 2-chloroethylenes with amidine of trifluoroacetic acid and benzamidine gave the 2,4,5-trisubstituted pyridines.
the reaction between 1-cyana-2-chlorotrifluoromethylene derivatives and amidines of trifluro- or trichioroacetic acids gives 2,4,5-trisubstituted pyridines.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the preparation of 2,4-disubstituted 5-cyanopyrimidines and the synthesis of 1-methyl (or 1-phenl)-6(1 H)-pyrimldineimines.
the synthesis of fluorine-containing pyrimidines with the 2,4,5-trisubstituted system.
the synthesis of fluorine-containing pyrimidine derivatives from 1-cyan-2-chlor-2-triflormethylethylen.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the condensation of 2-trichioromethylethylene and amidines of trifluroacetic acid gave the expected 2-trichlromethylpyrimidines, but the corresponding reaction of trifluoromethyethylenes with amidine of trifluoroacetic acid gave unexpected 2,4-ditrifluorometylpyrimidines.
all of the above reactions are of the Michael type, and the products are formed by the Michael addition of the amine component to the unsaturated system.
all the compounds obtained in this investigation are of great importance in the field of fluorine-containing heterocyclic chemistry.

The main takeaway from our work is that
1,1-disubstituted 1-cyanao-2-chlor-2-trifluroethylenes are good starting materials for the synthesis of tetrasubstitued pyrimidine derivatives.
2,4-disubstituted-6-amino-5-cyano- or -5-trifluoro-methylthio-pyrimidines are readily available in high yields from readily accessible starting materials.
we have shown that the reaction between 1-cyao-2-chlor-2-trifluro-methylethylene and amidines can give 5-amino- or 5-cyano-6-substituted pyrimidine derivatives.
